QF.id: AIFM CII Legal Documents and Negotiations_9

question.text: Ms. Neha Kapoor, LP at 'Aravalli India Growth III AIF', insists on a 'Most Favoured Nation' (MFN) clause in her side letter. What does an MFN clause in the AIF context primarily achieve for the holder?

answer.text: It allows Ms. Kapoor to receive side letter entitlements granted to other investors to protect herself from being placed in a less favourable position.
It entitles Ms. Kapoor to receive preferential management-fee rates lower than any Indian LP, with SEBI approval.
It gives Ms. Kapoor a priority claim in the distribution waterfall ahead of all other LPs.
It guarantees a preferred return or hurdle rate over and above what is offered in the PPM.

explanation.text: The Logic: An MFN clause allows an investor to receive side-letter entitlements granted to other investors, so she is not placed in a less favourable position than other current or future investors under the PPM or side-letter terms. It is a 'me-too' protection, not a fee or waterfall priority. The Trap: MFN does not touch waterfall priority or guarantee hurdle — those are primary commercial terms. SEBI approval is not the mechanism; MFN is a contractual LP-to-LP equality tool. Note: Workbook page 182 contains the MFN definition and side-letter context.
